Allegion (ALLE) is showing signs of an organic growth inflection that could support a higher valuation as improving volumes and stronger visibility into 2027 bolster expectations, BofA Securities said in a Friday note.

The company's Q3 Americas revenue rose 12%, with 9% organic growth driven by volume and pricing, while non-residential demand and data-center strength supported results, the firm noted. Adjusted earnings per share of $2.60 beat BofA's $2.48 estimate.

Management raised its 2026 organic growth outlook to 5% to 6% and adjusted EPS guidance to $9.05 to $9.10, prompting BofA to raise its 2026, 2027 and 2028 EPS estimates by 3%, 9% and 11%, respectively. The firm said its 2027 estimate is now 3% above consensus.

BofA upgraded its rating on the stock to buy from neutral and raised its price target to $200 from $164.

Key Takeaways

Bank of America stock fell 12.7% in the month through October 19 after a $1.21 billion regulatory penalty and disappointing third-quarter results.

Net interest income grew 8% to $16.4 billion, while average loans increased for the 10th consecutive quarter.

BAC traded near its five-year average price-to-tangible-book-value multiple, while analysts expected earnings growth through 2028.

The selloff could offer a buying opportunity, although compliance costs and weaker investment banking activity remain risks.

Bank of America (BAC:NYSE) stock declined 12.7% in the month through October 19, compared with a 0.6% gain for the S&P 500.

The selloff followed a major regulatory penalty and disappointing investment banking results, raising concerns about the bank's earnings outlook.

Why Did Bank of America Stock Fall?

On October 13, U.S. regulators announced more than $1.21 billion in penalties against Bank of America over anti-money-laundering and sanctions failures.

The bank subsequently reported a $1.2 billion regulatory settlement charge, reducing third-quarter earnings by $0.17 per share.

Excluding the charge, adjusted EPS reached $1.08, slightly below the $1.10 consensus estimate reported by TheFly.

Investment banking fees declined 11%, while fixed-income, currencies, and commodities trading revenue fell 17%.

However, net interest income increased 8% to $16.4 billion, supported by continued loan growth. CEO Brian Moynihan also indicated that net interest income growth could reach 8% or more in 2027.

Is BAC Stock Undervalued After Its Recent Decline?

At its October 19 closing price of $50.39, BAC traded at approximately 1.7 times tangible book value, near its five-year average and below its early-2022 peak of 2.3 times.

Bank of America (BAC): price/tangible book value, last 5 years (TIKR)

Ten analyst firms lowered their price targets following the results while maintaining their ratings. Meanwhile, Baird upgraded BAC to Outperform, arguing that the selloff had become excessive.

As of October 16, Wall Street's consensus target stood near $63, suggesting approximately 26% upside from the October 19 closing price.

Consensus estimates projected normalized EPS of approximately $4.51 in 2026, $5.19 in 2027, and $5.82 in 2028, representing roughly 15% growth in 2027 and another 12% in 2028.

Is BAC Stock a Sell or a Buying Opportunity?

Bank of America looks more like a buying opportunity than a stock investors need to sell after its recent decline.

The bank continues growing net interest income and its loan portfolio. However, compliance spending, weaker dealmaking activity, and a third-quarter CET1 ratio of 10.9% remain important risks.

For the first three, the broker expects modest beats and raises, with limited upside to gross margins and slight upside to revenues coming from data center/AI as well as Autos and Industrial. A common thread across the group is pricing.

BofA notes that better pricing for large OEMs, meaning flat to up 5% versus the traditional 1-5% price decline, is already expected, so any upside beyond that would come as a positive surprise.

STMicroelectronics is expected to deliver a modest beat and raise, with data center as the main storyline. BofA thinks the market may expect STM to lift its DC revenue guide to $3 billion for CY27, in line with BofA's own estimate, driven by Optical.

The harder question is margins. BofA believes investors need confidence that gross margins can move above 40% next year, which could come from mix, since BofA believes optical gross margins are above 50%, and/or from pricing for large OEMs.

Infineon also looks set for a modest beat and raise, and here the AI angle is about power. BofA thinks the market may expect IFX to guide combined FY27E AI and server CPU power revenues of €3.5-4 billion, while BofA's own estimate of €4.1 billion sits above the top of that range. Pricing is where the picture becomes more nuanced.

title: C's September Card Delinquencies Rise: Will This Impact Asset Quality?
detail:
C's September Card Delinquencies Rise: Will This Impact Asset Quality?
Zacks Equity Research
Fri, October 23, 2026 at 5:41 AM MST 3 min read
C
BAC
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup Inc. C continues to navigate credit-quality challenges amid an uncertain economic environment. According to its latest SEC filing, its subsidiary, Citibank N.A., reported higher credit card delinquencies and net principal losses in September 2026, while outstanding principal receivables declined during the month.

For the period ended Sept. 25, 2026, the Citibank Credit Card Master Trust I reported principal receivables of $18.7 billion, down from $19.1 billion at the beginning of the period. Receivables delinquent for 30 days or more increased to 1.35% in September from 1.29% in August, while those delinquent for 90 days or more rose to 0.65% from 0.63%. The Citibank Credit Card Issuance Trust's annualized net principal loss rate climbed to 2.18% from 2.03% in August and 1.90% in July, signaling a pickup in credit losses.

The detailed filing also showed that 97.3% of receivables were current in September. However, balances delinquent for 31-60 days were $80.7 million, while those delinquent for 151-180 days totaled $37.4 million. The portfolio's annualized gross yield was 25.03%, while the principal payment rate was 41.45%. Although the high portfolio yield provides a revenue cushion against credit losses, the increase in delinquencies and net principal losses warrants monitoring. These figures relate to the securitized credit card portfolios and should not be interpreted as representing Citigroup's entire loan portfolio.

Citigroup's broader asset-quality picture remains a concern. Although provisions for credit losses declined 2% year over year to $7.91 billion in the first nine months of 2026, the metric recorded a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.5% from 2022 to 2025. However, credit quality showed improvement in the third quarter, with the U.S. Cards net credit loss rate declining to 3.6% from 4.0% a year earlier. Management's earlier 2026 guidance projected a U.S. card net credit loss rate of 4-4.5%, highlighting continued credit risks.

Citigroup's organizational overhaul, business simplification initiatives and focus on operational efficiency could support profitability over the longer term. However, persistent inflation, pressure on borrowers' repayment capacity and rising card losses could weigh on asset quality. Any sustained deterioration in credit trends may lead to higher provisions and constrain earnings growth, even as the company benefits from resilient net interest income and a stronger focus on core businesses.
